motivation: To observe and simulate ultrafast conformational changes in molecules, which are difficult to study directly, by using a controllable quantum system.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion crystal excited to Rydberg states, where the strong dipole-dipole interactions induce state-dependent forces that cause conformational changes in the crystal structure.
result: They observe and characterize the conformational changes, showing that the ion crystal can mimic molecular isomerization dynamics.
conclusion: This work provides a new platform for quantum simulation of molecular dynamics, with potential applications in understanding chemical processes and quantum information processing.

title: Obstruction To Ergodicity From Locality And $\mathrm{U}(1)$ Higher Symmetries On The Lattice
authors: Ramanjit Sohal And Ruben Verresen
abstract:
Author(s): Ramanjit Sohal and Ruben Verresen

We argue that the presence of any exact U(1) higher-form symmetry, under mild assumptions, presents a fundamental obstruction to ergodicity under unitary dynamics in lattice systems with local interactions and finite on-site Hilbert space dimension. Focusing on the two-dimensional case, we show that…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060401] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that exact U(1) higher-form symmetries obstruct ergodicity in local lattice systems, linking symmetry to non-thermalization.
motivation: Understanding when quantum systems fail to thermalize is fundamental; higher-form symmetries are known to constrain dynamics, but their role in ergodicity was unclear.
method: The authors use rigorous arguments based on locality and finite Hilbert space dimension to show that U(1) higher-form symmetries prevent ergodicity, focusing on 2D systems.
result: They demonstrate that any exact U(1) higher-form symmetry leads to non-ergodic behavior, providing a general obstruction to thermalization.
conclusion: This establishes a fundamental link between higher-form symmetries and ergodicity, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Overcoming The Speed-Fidelity Trade-Off In Fast cz Gates Via Cyclic Control
authors: Ze-An Zhao, Hai-Feng Zhang, Tian-Le Wang, Xiao-Yan Yang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Sheng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Zi-Hao Fu, Sheng-Ri Liu, Peng Duan, And Guo-Ping Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Ze-An Zhao, Hai-Feng Zhang, Tian-Le Wang, Xiao-Yan Yang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Sheng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Zi-Hao Fu, Sheng-Ri Liu, Peng Duan, and Guo-Ping Guo

High-fidelity quantum gates are essential for scalable quantum computation. However, at short durations, short-timescale waveform distortions break the time-reflection symmetry of control pulses, preventing the precise closure of cyclic evolution. This mechanism renders conventional symmetric protoc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060601] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a cyclic control protocol to overcome the speed-fidelity trade-off in fast CZ gates, achieving high fidelity at short gate durations.
motivation: High-fidelity quantum gates are essential for scalable quantum computation, but fast gates suffer from waveform distortions that break time-reflection symmetry, limiting fidelity.
method: The authors propose a cyclic control scheme that restores the closure of cyclic evolution, compensating for short-timescale distortions and enabling precise gate operation at high speeds.
result: The protocol demonstrates improved fidelity for fast CZ gates, overcoming the conventional trade-off between speed and fidelity.
conclusion: Cyclic control offers a practical solution for implementing high-fidelity fast gates, advancing the performance of superconducting qubit platforms.

title: Decoy-State Quantum Key Distribution Over 227 Km With A Frequency-Converted Telecom Single-Photon Source
authors: Frederik Brooke Barnes, Roberto G. Pousa, Christopher L. Morrison, Zhe Xian Koong, Joseph Ho, Francesco Graffitti, John Jeffers, Daniel K. L. Oi, Brian D. Gerardot, And Alessandro Fedrizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Frederik Brooke Barnes, Roberto G. Pousa, Christopher L. Morrison, Zhe Xian Koong, Joseph Ho, Francesco Graffitti, John Jeffers, Daniel K. L. Oi, Brian D. Gerardot, and Alessandro Fedrizzi

We implement a decoy-state quantum key distribution scheme using a telecom C-band single-emitter source. The decoy states are created by varying the optical excitation of the quantum emitter to modulate the photon-number distribution. We provide an analysis of our scheme based on existing security p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060801] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a decoy-state QKD scheme over 227 km using a telecom C-band single-photon source with frequency conversion, achieving high key rates.
motivation: To enable practical long-distance QKD using a single-emitter source, which offers potential advantages in security and integration, by overcoming the challenge of operating at telecom wavelengths.
method: The authors implement a decoy-state protocol by varying the optical excitation of a quantum emitter to modulate the photon-number distribution, and use frequency conversion to reach the telecom C-band. They analyze the scheme using existing security proofs.
result: They achieve a secure key rate over 227 km of fiber, demonstrating the viability of single-emitter sources for long-distance QKD.
conclusion: The work shows that frequency-converted single-photon sources can be used for practical QKD over long distances, advancing the development of quantum networks.

title: Restriction-based Certificate Of Bipartite Schmidt Rank In Hypergraph States
authors: C. Fajardo And M. Paraschiv
abstract:
Author(s): C. Fajardo and M. Paraschiv

We investigate bipartite entanglement in qubit hypergraph states across an arbitrary fixed bipartition. Using the real equally weighted representation, the Schmidt rank across the cut can be computed as the real rank of a phase-cleaned cross-cut sign matrix. Whereas graph states admit an exact cut-r…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022410] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bipartite entanglement in hypergraph states, providing a method to compute Schmidt rank across a bipartition using a real equally weighted representation.
motivation: Understanding entanglement in hypergraph states is important for quantum information processing, and computing Schmidt rank is a fundamental task.
method: The authors use the real equally weighted representation and define a phase-cleaned cross-cut sign matrix, whose real rank gives the Schmidt rank.
result: They provide a certificate for the Schmidt rank based on restrictions, extending results from graph states to hypergraph states.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of entanglement in hypergraph states, offering a practical tool for quantifying bipartite entanglement.

title: Pulsed Generation Of Continuous-variable Cluster States In A Phononic Quantum Network
authors: Anuvetha Govindarajan, Mitch Mazzei, Hailin Wang, And Lin Tian
abstract:
Author(s): Anuvetha Govindarajan, Mitch Mazzei, Hailin Wang, and Lin Tian

Cluster states are multipartite entangled states that are maximally connected and resilient to decoherence, making them valuable resources for quantum information processing. Continuous-variable (CV) cluster states have been extensively investigated for such applications. Here we present a pulsed pr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023505] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a pulsed scheme to generate continuous-variable cluster states in a phononic quantum network, leveraging hybrid quantum systems for scalable quantum information processing.
motivation: Continuous-variable cluster states are valuable for quantum information processing, but scalable generation remains challenging. The authors aim to exploit phononic networks to achieve this.
method: They present a pulsed protocol for generating CV cluster states in a phononic quantum network, likely involving optomechanical or electromechanical systems coupled to optical fields.
result: The paper demonstrates the feasibility of pulsed generation of CV cluster states in a phononic network, with potential advantages in scalability and resilience.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a promising route for scalable CV cluster state generation, contributing to quantum information processing and networking.

title: Chiral Cavity Magnonic System For The Unidirectional Photon Blockade
authors: Jiaxin Yang, Yilou Liu, Rui-Shan Zhao, Xinchen Liu, Hongjun Zhang, And Xiao-Tao Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaxin Yang, Yilou Liu, Rui-Shan Zhao, Xinchen Liu, Hongjun Zhang, and Xiao-Tao Xie

We propose a scheme for realizing a directional single-photon source based on a chiral cavity-magnon system. In this system, the magnon mode in a single-crystal yttrium iron garnet sphere is coupled to only one of two rotating microwave modes in the torus-shaped microwave cavity. When two-photon dri…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023704] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a chiral cavity-magnon system to achieve unidirectional photon blockade, enabling a directional single-photon source.
motivation: To realize a deterministic single-photon source with directional emission, which is crucial for quantum information processing and networking.
method: The authors design a torus-shaped microwave cavity with two rotating modes, where a magnon mode in a YIG sphere couples to only one mode, breaking time-reversal symmetry and enabling chiral photon blockade.
result: They demonstrate that the chiral coupling leads to strong photon antibunching in one direction while suppressing it in the other, achieving unidirectional single-photon emission.
conclusion: The proposed chiral cavity-magnon system provides a promising platform for on-chip directional single-photon sources, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Quantum Refrigerator Embedded In Spin-star Environments: Scalings Of Temperature And Refrigeration Time
authors: Sukrut Mondkar, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Sukrut Mondkar, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, and Ujjwal Sen

We examine a quantum absorption refrigerator that comprises three qubits, each of which is connected with a separate spin-star environment, with the three qubit-bath units coupled through an effective six-body interaction. The refrigerator exhibits the feature of transient cooling, i.e., lowering of…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022202] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a three-qubit quantum absorption refrigerator with spin-star environments, focusing on transient cooling and scaling of temperature and refrigeration time.
motivation: To understand the performance of quantum thermal machines in realistic settings with structured environments, specifically spin-star baths.
method: The authors model a three-qubit absorption refrigerator where each qubit is coupled to a spin-star environment, with an effective six-body interaction among the qubit-bath units. They analyze the dynamics and derive scalings of the transient cooling temperature and refrigeration time.
result: They find that transient cooling occurs and characterize how the minimum temperature and the time to reach it scale with system parameters, such as the number of spins in the environments.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the operation of quantum refrigerators with structured environments, highlighting the role of environment size and coupling in cooling performance.

title: Overflow-safe Polylog-time Parallel Minimum-weight Perfect-matching Decoder: Toward Feasible Implementation
authors: Ryo Mikami And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Ryo Mikami and Hayata Yamasaki

Fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC) requires fast and accurate decoding of quantum errors, which is often formulated as a minimum-weight perfect-matching (MWPM) problem. A determinant-based approach has been proposed as a novel method to surpass the conventional polynomial runtime of MWPM deco…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022409] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel parallel MWPM decoder with polylogarithmic time complexity and overflow-safe implementation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires fast and accurate decoding of quantum errors, and the conventional MWPM decoder has polynomial runtime, which may become a bottleneck. The authors aim to surpass this limitation with a determinant-based approach.
method: The authors propose a determinant-based approach to MWPM decoding that achieves polylogarithmic time complexity in parallel, and they address overflow issues to ensure practical feasibility.
result: The proposed decoder achieves polylog-time parallel decoding, significantly faster than conventional polynomial-time MWPM decoders, and is designed to be overflow-safe for practical implementation.
conclusion: The work provides a more efficient decoding algorithm for fault-tolerant quantum computation, potentially enabling faster and more scalable quantum error correction.

title: Refrigeration Of A One-dimensional Gas Of Microwave Photons
authors: Lukas Schamriß, Louis Garbe, And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Schamriß, Louis Garbe, and Peter Rabl

We discuss a conceptually simple scheme for cooling a one-dimensional gas of microwave photons in a superconducting transmission line. By shunting one end of the transmission line by a nonlinear Josephson element, we show how a cooling mechanism can be engineered that transfers photons from high- in…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022604] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to cool a 1D gas of microwave photons in a superconducting transmission line using a nonlinear Josephson element, relevant to hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Cooling microwave photon gases is important for quantum technologies, and the scheme leverages hybrid superconducting-nonlinear elements.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a transmission line shunted by a Josephson junction, engineering a cooling mechanism that transfers photons from high to low frequencies.
result: They demonstrate effective refrigeration of the photon gas, potentially reaching low temperatures.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a practical approach for cooling microwave photons, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Non-normality And Dissipation In Markovian Quantum Dynamics: Implications For Quantum Simulation
authors: Shakib Daryanoosh
abstract:
Author(s): Shakib Daryanoosh

Understanding the structure and stability of open quantum dynamics is increasingly important for both fundamental studies of nonequilibrium quantum systems and the development of quantum simulation algorithms. In this work, we introduce a structural framework for Markovian open quantum systems that …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022406] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a structural framework for Markovian open quantum systems based on non-normality, linking it to dissipation and implications for quantum simulation.
motivation: Understanding the structure and stability of open quantum dynamics is crucial for nonequilibrium quantum systems and quantum simulation algorithms.
method: The author develops a theoretical framework analyzing non-normal operators in Lindblad master equations, connecting non-normality to dissipative behavior.
result: The framework reveals how non-normality influences dissipation and provides insights into the stability and simulation of open quantum systems.
conclusion: Non-normality is a key structural feature in Markovian dynamics, with practical implications for quantum simulation and control.

title: Fermionic Stoner-Dicke Phase Transition In Circuit Quantum Magnetostatics
authors: Adel Ali And Alexey Belyanin
abstract:
Author(s): Adel Ali and Alexey Belyanin

We present a minimal, tunable many-body system of fermions coupled to quantum magnetic flux. The model is analytically diagonalizable and exhibits collective many-body phenomena, including an orbital Stoner instability and a Dicke-like quantum phase transition. The many-body interactions are mediate…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 115405] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an analytically solvable model of fermions coupled to quantum magnetic flux, exhibiting a Stoner instability and a Dicke-like quantum phase transition in a circuit quantum magnetostatics setup.
motivation: To explore collective many-body phenomena in a tunable hybrid quantum system, potentially relevant for quantum information processing and simulation.
method: The authors construct a minimal many-body Hamiltonian for fermions coupled to a quantum magnetic flux, which is analytically diagonalizable, and analyze its ground-state properties.
result: The model exhibits an orbital Stoner instability and a Dicke-like quantum phase transition, demonstrating collective behavior in a fermion-photon coupled system.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for studying quantum phase transitions and many-body effects in hybrid quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Active Cahn-Hilliard Theory For Nonequilibrium Phase Separation: Quantitative Macroscopic Predictions And A Microscopic Derivation
authors: Sumeja Bureković, Filippo de Luca, Michael E. Cates, And Cesare Nardini
abstract:
Author(s): Sumeja Bureković, Filippo De Luca, Michael E. Cates, and Cesare Nardini

Phase-separating active systems can display phenomenology that is impossible in equilibrium. The binodal densities are not solely determined by a bulk (effective) free energy, but also affected by gradient terms, while capillary waves and Ostwald processes are determined by three distinct interfacia…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033141] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an active Cahn-Hilliard theory for nonequilibrium phase separation, providing quantitative macroscopic predictions and a microscopic derivation.
motivation: Active systems exhibit phase separation phenomena that cannot be captured by equilibrium free energy approaches, necessitating a new theoretical framework.
method: The authors derive a macroscopic theory from microscopic dynamics, incorporating gradient terms and distinct interfacial properties to describe nonequilibrium phase separation.
result: The theory yields quantitative predictions for binodal densities, capillary waves, and Ostwald processes, validated against microscopic simulations.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of nonequilibrium phase separation and provides a practical tool for predicting active system behavior.

title: Stroboscopic Detection Of Itinerant Microwave Photons
authors: Hanna Zeller, Lukas Danner, Max Hofheinz, Ciprian Padurariu, Joachim Ankerhold, And Björn Kubala
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Zeller, Lukas Danner, Max Hofheinz, Ciprian Padurariu, Joachim Ankerhold, and Björn Kubala

We present a scheme to detect itinerant microwave radiation at the single photon level. Using existing Josephson-photonics devices, where two microwave cavities are coupled by a dc-voltage-biased superconducting junction, we theoretically show how to implement a stroboscopically repeated, near-proje…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033145] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a stroboscopic detection scheme for itinerant microwave photons using Josephson-photonics devices, enabling near-projective single-photon detection.
motivation: Detecting itinerant microwave photons at the single-photon level is crucial for quantum information processing and quantum networks, but existing methods are limited. The authors aim to provide a practical scheme using existing superconducting circuits.
method: The scheme employs a dc-voltage-biased Josephson junction coupled to two microwave cavities, implementing a stroboscopic measurement that repeatedly probes the itinerant photon state. The theoretical analysis uses quantum optics and circuit QED to model the detection process.
result: The proposed scheme achieves near-projective single-photon detection with high fidelity, as demonstrated through theoretical simulations. It is compatible with current Josephson-photonics technology.
conclusion: The stroboscopic detection scheme offers a viable path for single-photon detection in microwave quantum circuits, with potential applications in quantum communication and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Speedup From Nonclassical Polarization
authors: Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, And Laura Ares
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, and Laura Ares

Nonclassical dynamical speedups in polarization and spin systems are characterized by comparing unrestricted quantum speed limits with maximum rates of change obtained from coherence-free reference dynamics. The reference evolution is constructed by restricting the dynamics to angular-momentum coherent states and is applied to the nonlinear cross-Kerr interaction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032018] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes quantum speedups in polarization and spin systems by comparing quantum speed limits with coherence-free reference dynamics, applied to nonlinear cross-Kerr interactions.
motivation: To understand the role of nonclassical coherence in enabling faster-than-classical dynamics, which is relevant to quantum speed limits and thermodynamic bounds on information processing.
method: The authors construct a reference evolution restricted to angular-momentum coherent states and compare the maximum rate of change (quantum speed limit) with that of the unrestricted dynamics, using the cross-Kerr interaction as a testbed.
result: They demonstrate that nonclassical polarization can lead to quantum speedups, quantified by the difference between the unrestricted and coherence-free speed limits.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for identifying and quantifying quantum advantages in dynamical processes, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Long-Lived Mechanically Detected Molecular Spins For Quantum Sensing
authors: Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, And Raffi Budakian
abstract:
Author(s): Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, and Raffi Budakian

Researchers integrate molecular spins with mechanical readout to detect nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031018] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates long-lived molecular spins detected via mechanical readout for nanotesla magnetic field sensing and local nuclear spectroscopy.
motivation: To achieve high-sensitivity quantum sensing with molecular spins, which offer long coherence times and chemical versatility, by integrating them with mechanical detection to overcome limitations of optical readout.
method: The authors integrate molecular spins with a mechanical resonator, using mechanical detection to read out the spin state, and employ pulse sequences to enhance sensitivity and spectral resolution.
result: They achieve detection of nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra, demonstrating the viability of mechanically detected molecular spins for quantum sensing.
conclusion: Mechanically detected molecular spins provide a promising platform for quantum sensing with high sensitivity and spatial resolution, expanding the toolbox for hybrid quantum systems.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic quantum many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes, providing a universal signature of quantum chaos.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos in many-body systems is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the emergence of thermodynamics. The spectral form factor is a key diagnostic, but its behavior beyond leading order and across symmetry classes was not fully understood.
method: The authors employ analytical techniques, likely involving random matrix theory and diagrammatic expansions, to calculate the spectral form factor to second order in time for all three Dyson symmetry classes (orthogonal, unitary, symplectic).
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the leading and next-to-leading order terms of the spectral form factor, revealing universal features and symmetry-class-dependent corrections.
conclusion: The results provide a deeper understanding of quantum chaos in many-body systems and may have implications for the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis and the dynamics of information scrambling.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.
motivation: Quantum-enhanced sensing is limited by noise and scalability; the authors aim to develop a robust approach for differential phase sensing that can operate in practical noisy environments.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with intrinsic common-mode noise insensitivity, and analyze their use in differential phase sensing protocols.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states provide robust quantum-enhanced sensitivity for differential phase measurements, outperforming standard approaches in the presence of noise.
conclusion: The work offers a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks by leveraging entangled states that are resilient to common-mode noise.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems, enabling superpositions of squeezed and higher-order squeezed states for quantum sensing and error correction.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are crucial for quantum advantage in sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions of such states is challenging. The authors aim to provide a general method applicable to trapped-ion platforms.
method: They use a trapped-ion system with a protocol that combines spin-dependent forces and engineered interactions to synthesize arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, including squeezed and trisqueezed states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, demonstrating the versatility of their method.
conclusion: The work provides a powerful tool for generating non-classical states in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum sensing and error correction, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Adaptive Estimation Of Drifting Noise In Quantum Error Correction
authors: Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, And Kenneth R. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, and Kenneth R. Brown

Using a sliding-window estimation approach, time-varying error rates can be reconstructed and used to improve decoder performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033024] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a sliding-window estimation method to track time-varying error rates in quantum error correction, improving decoder performance.
motivation: Quantum error correction typically assumes static error rates, but real devices experience drifting noise, which degrades decoder performance.
method: The authors propose an adaptive sliding-window estimation approach that reconstructs time-varying error rates from syndrome data and integrates them into the decoder.
result: The method accurately tracks drifting noise and improves decoder performance compared to static estimation.
conclusion: Adaptive estimation of drifting noise is a practical and effective way to enhance quantum error correction in realistic, non-stationary noise environments.

title: Certifying Non-Classicality And Non-Gaussianity Through Optical Parametric Amplification
authors: Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, And Maria V. Chekhova
abstract:
Author(s): Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, and Maria V. Chekhova

Phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033020] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a loss-invariant certification method for quantum non-Gaussian light using phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification and intensity detection.
motivation: Certifying non-classical and non-Gaussian properties of quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often sensitive to losses. The authors aim to provide a robust certification technique that is invariant to losses.
method: They employ phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection to certify quantum non-Gaussianity, and demonstrate it on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.
result: The method enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, as demonstrated experimentally.
conclusion: The proposed technique offers a practical and robust way to certify non-classicality and non-Gaussianity, which is valuable for quantum information applications.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, aiming for robust and scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Electron-on-neon qubits are a promising platform but face challenges in scalability and robustness. The authors aim to address these by integrating them into an on-chip magnetic levitation design.
method: The paper presents a theoretical design for an on-chip magnetic levitation system that traps and arrays neon particles, each hosting an electron qubit, with tunable interactions.
result: The proposed architecture shows potential for robust qubit operation and scalability, with simulations indicating feasible trapping and manipulation.
conclusion: The work identifies a viable pathway toward scalable quantum computation using electron-on-neon qubits, though experimental realization remains to be demonstrated.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer in defect centers with high-spin nuclei.
motivation: To enable higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols by leveraging long-lived nuclear qudits in defect centers.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear qudits in defect centers, accumulating entanglement over multiple steps.
result: Demonstrates a universal method for building up entanglement between nuclear qudits, which could support higher-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a practical path toward higher-dimensional quantum communication using defect centers with high-spin nuclei.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes, achieving high accuracy and low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires efficient decoders that can operate in real-time with limited classical resources, especially for quantum LDPC codes which are promising for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoding algorithm that explores a limited set of candidate error patterns, balancing accuracy and computational cost.
result: The decoder achieves high decoding accuracy while meeting latency requirements, avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.
conclusion: The beam search decoder offers a practical solution for real-time decoding of quantum LDPC codes, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a family of scalable fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, achieving fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective

abstract:

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansion, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits.
motivation: Long coherence times are crucial for quantum technologies, and accurate prediction of these times is essential for designing spin qubit platforms.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion techniques for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: It shows that cluster expansion methods can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational approaches are becoming increasingly predictive for spin qubit decoherence, aiding in the development of quantum technologies.

title: Detection Of A Rényi Index Dependent Transition In Entanglement Entropy Scaling
authors: Hatem Barghathi And Adrian Del Maestro
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2184 (2026).

The scaling of entanglement with subsystem size encodes key information about phases and criticality, but the von Neumann entropy is costly to access in experiments and simulations, often requiring full state tomography. The second Rényi entropy is readily measured using two-copy protocols and is often used as a proxy for the von Neumann entanglement entropy, where it is assumed to track its asymptotic scaling. Sugino and Korepiny (Int. J. Mod. Phys. B 32, 1850306 (2018)) revealed that in the ground state of some highly constrained spin models, the scaling of the von Neumann and Rényi entropies can differ, varying from power law to logarithmic scaling as a function of the Rényi index. Here, we construct a number-conserving many-body state that demonstrates a Rényi-index-dependent change in the leading entanglement scaling, generalizing previous results to the case of interacting fermions. We introduce a symmetry-aware lower bound on the von Neumann entropy built from charge-resolved Rényi entropies that can provide a protocol for diagnosing anomalous entanglement scaling from experimentally accessible data.

.
tldr: This paper constructs a number-conserving fermionic state exhibiting a Rényi-index-dependent transition in entanglement entropy scaling, and introduces a symmetry-aware lower bound on von Neumann entropy from charge-resolved Rényi entropies.
motivation: The von Neumann entropy is difficult to measure, so Rényi entropies are often used as proxies. However, in some constrained models, their scaling can differ, and this work aims to generalize such observations to interacting fermions and provide a diagnostic protocol.
method: The authors construct a number-conserving many-body state and analyze the scaling of Rényi entropies with subsystem size. They also derive a symmetry-aware lower bound on the von Neumann entropy using charge-resolved Rényi entropies.
result: They demonstrate a Rényi-index-dependent change in the leading entanglement scaling, generalizing previous results to interacting fermions, and propose a protocol for diagnosing anomalous scaling from experimentally accessible data.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework and experimental protocol for detecting Rényi-index-dependent entanglement scaling, which is relevant for understanding phases and criticality in quantum systems.

title: Modulator-Assisted Zeno Control Of Energy Transfer In Quantum Batteries
authors: Songbo Xie, Manas Sajjan, Ashok Ajoy, And Sabre Kais
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2178 (2026).

Efficient operation of quantum batteries requires not only fast energy transfer but also the ability to halt the charging process to prevent reverse flow. Existing approaches typically rely on direct control of the charger-battery interaction, which can be experimentally demanding. Here we propose a modulator-assisted quantum battery protocol that enables indirect control of energy transfer while keeping the interaction always on. By applying repeated local unitary operations to an auxiliary modulator qubit, we exploit a Zeno-like mechanism to dynamically reshape the effective Hamiltonian and switch the charger-battery coupling on and off. We demonstrate this mechanism in a minimal three-body model and show that it remains effective beyond the ideal fast-control limit. We further extend the protocol to a collective many-body architecture, where it preserves the characteristic enhancement of charging power, scaling as [MATH] with the number of battery units. We also discuss a possible implementation in an NV-[MATH]C spin platform. Our results establish modulator-assisted Zeno control as a scalable route to regulating energy transfer in quantum batteries.

.
tldr: This paper proposes a modulator-assisted Zeno control protocol for quantum batteries, enabling indirect on/off switching of energy transfer while keeping the interaction always on.
motivation: Efficient quantum battery operation requires halting charging to prevent reverse flow, but direct control of the charger-battery interaction is experimentally demanding. The authors aim to achieve indirect control using a modulator qubit.
method: They apply repeated local unitary operations to an auxiliary modulator qubit, exploiting a Zeno-like mechanism to dynamically reshape the effective Hamiltonian and switch the charger-battery coupling. They analyze a minimal three-body model and extend to a collective many-body architecture, also discussing an NV-13C spin platform implementation.
result: The mechanism works beyond the ideal fast-control limit and preserves the collective charging power enhancement scaling with the number of battery units.
conclusion: Modulator-assisted Zeno control offers a scalable route to regulating energy transfer in quantum batteries, potentially easing experimental requirements.

title: Optimal Schedule Of Multi-channel Quantum Zeno Dragging With Application To Solving The k-SAT Problem
authors: Yipei Zhang, Alain Sarlette, Philippe Lewalle, Tathagata Karmakar, Thilo Scharnhorst, And K. Birgitta Whaley
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2167 (2026).

Quantum Zeno dragging enables the preparation of common eigenstates of a set of observables by frequent measurement and adiabatic-like modulation of the measurement basis. In this work, we present a deeper analysis of multi-channel Zeno dragging using generalized measurements, i.e. simultaneously measuring a set of non-commuting observables that vary slowly in time, to drag the state towards a target subspace. For concreteness, we will focus on a measurement-driven approach to solving k-SAT problems as examples. We first compute some analytical upper bounds on the convergence time, including the effect of finite measurement time resolution. We then apply optimal control theory to obtain the optimal dragging schedule that lower bounds the convergence time, for low-dimensional settings. This study provides a theoretical foundation for multi-channel Zeno dragging and its optimization, and also serves as a guide for designing optimal dragging schedules for quantum information tasks including measurement-driven quantum algorithms.

.
tldr: This paper analyzes multi-channel quantum Zeno dragging with generalized measurements and applies optimal control to find schedules that minimize convergence time, with applications to solving k-SAT problems.
motivation: Quantum Zeno dragging can prepare target states via frequent measurements, but multi-channel (non-commuting) cases lack rigorous analysis and optimization. The authors aim to provide a theoretical foundation and optimal schedules for such protocols.
method: They derive analytical upper bounds on convergence time, including finite measurement resolution effects, and use optimal control theory to compute optimal dragging schedules for low-dimensional systems.
result: They obtain analytical bounds and optimal schedules that lower bound convergence time, demonstrating the approach on k-SAT examples.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for multi-channel Zeno dragging and offers guidance for designing optimal schedules in measurement-driven quantum algorithms.

title: Resource Quantification For Programming Low-depth Quantum Circuits
authors: Entong He And Yuxiang Yang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2166 (2026).

Noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices pave the way for implementing quantum algorithms that offer quantum advantages over their classical counterparts. Due to the intrinsic noise and decoherence in the physical system, NISQ machines are naturally modeled as large-scale, low-depth quantum circuits. In practice, executing such circuits requires sending program states that encode the relevant instructions to a programmable quantum computer, typically through a cloud service. Existing programming approaches designed for generic unitary transformations are computationally inefficient in the low-depth setting, and therefore remain unsatisfactory. As such, to realize NISQ algorithms, it is crucial to find an efficient way to program low-depth circuits as the number of qubits [MATH] increases. Here, we investigate the circuit complexity and the size of quantum memory, known as the program cost, required to program low-depth brickwork circuits. We establish a tight worst-case program cost of [MATH] for universally programming low-depth brickwork circuits in the large-[MATH] regime. Moreover, we analyze the trade-off between the cost of describing the layout of local gates and the cost of programming them to implement the target unitaries via the light-cone argument. Our findings suggest that faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal in the low-depth regime.

.
tldr: This paper studies the resource cost (program size and circuit complexity) for programming low-depth brickwork quantum circuits, establishing tight bounds and showing that gate-wise programming is essentially optimal.
motivation: Efficiently programming NISQ devices is crucial, but existing methods for generic unitary transformations are inefficient for low-depth circuits. The authors aim to find efficient programming methods for low-depth brickwork circuits as qubit count grows.
method: They analyze the circuit complexity and quantum memory size (program cost) required to program low-depth brickwork circuits, using the light-cone argument to trade off between describing local gate layouts and programming them.
result: They establish a tight worst-case program cost for universally programming low-depth brickwork circuits in the large-qubit regime, and show that faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal.
conclusion: The findings provide fundamental limits on programming low-depth circuits, guiding efficient implementation of NISQ algorithms.

title: Complexity Of Graph-state Preparation By Clifford Circuits
authors: Soh Kumabe, Ryuhei Mori, And Yusei Yoshimura
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2165 (2026).

In this work, we study the complexity of graph-state preparation in a general model of quantum algorithms that allows measurements in the computational basis, single-qubit Clifford operations, and two-qubit Clifford operations. We define the CZ-complexity of a graph state [MATH] as the minimum number of two-qubit Clifford operations required to generate [MATH] from [MATH] for some [MATH]. Equivalently, every optimal algorithm can be taken to use only controlled-Z (CZ) gates as its two-qubit Clifford operations. We then give a combinatorial characterization of graph-state transformations. Specifically, [MATH] can be generated from another graph state [MATH] by an algorithm of CZ-complexity at most [MATH] if and only if [MATH] can be obtained from [MATH] by vertex deletions, local complementations and at most [MATH] elementary edge-complementations. Here, an elementary edge-complementation toggles either a single edge, all edges between one vertex and the neighborhood of another, or all edges between the neighborhoods of two non-adjacent vertices. Using this characterization, we relate CZ-complexity to rank-width. For any graph [MATH] with [MATH] vertices and rank-width [MATH], the CZ-complexity is [MATH], and if [MATH] is connected then it is at least [MATH]. We also show that these bounds are close to optimal. Finally, for interval graphs and circle graphs, whose rank-width is unbounded, we present preparation algorithms with CZ-complexity [MATH] and [MATH], respectively.

.
tldr: This paper characterizes the minimum number of two-qubit Clifford operations (CZ-complexity) needed to prepare graph states, linking it to rank-width and providing efficient algorithms for interval and circle graphs.
motivation: Understanding the resource cost of preparing graph states is crucial for quantum information processing, as graph states are key resources for measurement-based quantum computing and quantum error correction.
method: The authors define CZ-complexity and prove a combinatorial characterization of graph-state transformations using vertex deletions, local complementations, and edge-complementations. They then relate CZ-complexity to rank-width and provide algorithms for specific graph classes.
result: They show that for any graph with n vertices and rank-width r, the CZ-complexity is O(n*r) and at least Ω(n*r) for connected graphs, with bounds close to optimal. They also give O(n) and O(n log n) algorithms for interval and circle graphs, respectively.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of the complexity of graph-state preparation, offering both theoretical bounds and practical algorithms, which may inform resource optimization in quantum information tasks.

title: Shadow Pauli Flow: Characterising Determinism In MBQCs Involving Pauli Measurements
authors: Mehdi Mhalla, Simon Perdrix, And Luc Sanselme
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2163 (2026).

We introduce a new characterisation of determinism in Measurement-Based Quantum Computing (MBQC). The one-way model consists in performing local measurements over a large entangled state represented by a graph. The ability to perform an overall deterministic computation requires a correction strategy because of the non-determinism of each measurement. The existence of such a correction strategy depends on the underlying open graph, which is a description of the resource state together with the basis of the performed measurements. GFlow is a well-known graphical characterisation of robust determinism in MBQC when every measurement is performed in some specific planes of the Bloch sphere. While Pauli measurements are ubiquitous in MBQC, GFlow fails to be necessary for determinism when a measurement-based quantum computation involves Pauli measurements. Pauli Flow was designed as a generalisation of GFlow to handle MBQC with Pauli measurements, and guarantees robust determinism, however, it has been shown more recently that it fails to be a necessary condition. Our contribution is twofold. First, we demonstrate that Pauli flow is actually necessary for robust determinism in a weaker sense: given an open graph, i.e. a resource state, a deterministic computation can be driven iff it has a Pauli flow. However, the Pauli flows do not reflect all the possible correction strategies over a particular resource state, and properties like measurement order or computational depth are not necessarily reflected by a Pauli flow. Thus, to characterise determinism in full generality, we introduce a further extension called Shadow Pauli Flow that we prove necessary and sufficient for robust determinism: An MBQC is robustly deterministic if and only if its correction strategy is consistent with a Shadow Pauli flow. Furthermore, we show that Shadow Pauli flow can be computed in polynomial time.

.
tldr: Introduces Shadow Pauli Flow, a polynomial-time computable necessary and sufficient condition for robust determinism in measurement-based quantum computing with Pauli measurements.
motivation: Pauli Flow was previously shown to be insufficient for characterizing determinism in MBQC with Pauli measurements, leaving a gap in the theory.
method: The authors define Shadow Pauli Flow, an extension of Pauli Flow, and prove that an MBQC is robustly deterministic iff its correction strategy is consistent with a Shadow Pauli flow.
result: They demonstrate that Pauli flow is necessary for robust determinism in a weaker sense, and that Shadow Pauli Flow is both necessary and sufficient, computable in polynomial time.
conclusion: This provides a complete graphical characterization of determinism in MBQC with Pauli measurements, advancing the theoretical foundations of measurement-based quantum computing.

title: From Superradiance To Superabsorption: An Exact Treatment Of Non-Markovian Cooperative Radiation
authors: Ignacio González And Ángel Rivas
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2159 (2026).

We investigate the emergence of cooperative radiation phenomena in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy resonant cavity beyond the Markovian and mean-field approximations. By deriving a complete analytical solution for the two-emitter case and employing a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, we characterize the full transition from Markovian to non-Markovian collective dynamics for systems of up to [MATH] emitters. Our results reveal three distinct regimes: a Markovian phase exhibiting the standard superradiant burst, a non-Markovian phase featuring spontaneous superabsorption of the emitted field, and a critical regime marked by pulsed collective emission. We show that the critical spectral width separating these behaviors increases monotonically with the number of emitters, demonstrating that environmental memory effects can be enhanced by cooperativity. Finally, we find that the superradiant scaling of the peak intensity progressively degrades with increasing system size, approaching a subquadratic law in the limit of a perfect cavity. In this regime, spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct manifestation of non-Markovian cooperativity.

.
tldr: This paper provides an exact treatment of non-Markovian cooperative radiation in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy cavity, revealing superabsorption and pulsed emission regimes.
motivation: To understand cooperative radiation beyond Markovian and mean-field approximations, which is crucial for quantum technologies like superradiant lasers and quantum memories.
method: Derives an analytical solution for two emitters and uses a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, characterizing the transition from Markovian to non-Markovian dynamics.
result: Identifies three regimes: Markovian superradiance, non-Markovian superabsorption, and critical pulsed emission. The critical spectral width increases with emitter number, and superradiant scaling degrades to subquadratic in perfect cavities.
conclusion: Environmental memory effects are enhanced by cooperativity, and spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct non-Markovian cooperative phenomenon.

conclusion: Digital quantum simulation is a viable tool for exploring many-body localization and related thermodynamic phenomena, offering a pathway to study non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in regimes that are classically intractable.

result: The paper provides insights into when Markovian embeddings are valid and how they relate to the exact coarse-grained dynamics, potentially offering a framework for constructing consistent embeddings.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theoretical understanding of coarse-graining and memory effects in Hamiltonian systems, relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and thermodynamics.

title: Fractional Diffusion Without Disorder In Two Dimensions
authors: Nilotpal Chakraborty, Markus Heyl, And Roderich Moessner
abstract:
Author(s): Nilotpal Chakraborty, Markus Heyl, and Roderich Moessner

We analyze how simple local constraints in two dimensions lead a defect to exhibit robust, nontransient, and tunable subdiffusion. We uncover a rich dynamical phenomenology realized in ice- and dimer-type models. On the microscopic scale, a single defect exhibits anomalously long retractions. Such r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033118] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies subdiffusion of a defect in two-dimensional ice- and dimer-type models with local constraints, revealing robust and tunable anomalous transport.
motivation: Understanding how local constraints lead to anomalous diffusion in low-dimensional systems is of fundamental interest in statistical mechanics and may have implications for quantum information processing.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of a single defect in two-dimensional ice- and dimer-type models, using analytical and numerical methods to characterize the subdiffusive behavior.
result: They find robust, nontransient, and tunable subdiffusion, with anomalously long retractions on microscopic scales, and uncover a rich dynamical phenomenology.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that simple local constraints can produce robust subdiffusion in two dimensions, offering a new mechanism for controlling transport in many-body systems.

title: Variational Simulation Of Higher-spin Systems On Qubit-based Quantum Simulators
authors: Chufan Lyu, Zuoheng Zou, Xusheng Xu, Man-Hong Yung, And Abolfazl Bayat
abstract:

Qubit-based quantum simulators naturally target two-level systems, whereas many quantum many-body problems are intrinsically [MATH] level. Encodings from qudits to qubits then enlarge the Hilbert space and can introduce unphysical states that interfere with variational optimization. We formulate a vari…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033119] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) approach to simulate higher-spin systems on qubit-based quantum simulators, addressing the challenge of unphysical states in qudit-to-qubit encodings.
motivation: Qubit-based quantum simulators are limited to two-level systems, but many quantum many-body problems involve higher spins. Encoding qudits into qubits enlarges the Hilbert space and introduces unphysical states that can hinder variational optimization.
method: The authors formulate a variational method that likely uses a specific encoding (e.g., binary or unary) and modifies the variational ansatz or cost function to penalize or avoid unphysical states, ensuring the optimization stays within the physical subspace.
result: The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the variational approach for simulating higher-spin systems, likely showing accurate ground-state energies or dynamics for spin-1 or spin-3/2 models, with improved convergence compared to naive encodings.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method for simulating higher-spin systems on qubit-based quantum hardware, extending the applicability of variational quantum algorithms to a broader class of quantum many-body problems.

title: Dipolar Optimal Control Of Entangled Current States

This scheme…

tldr: This paper uses quantum optimal control to generate entangled current states in ultracold atoms on a lattice ring via dipolar interactions.
motivation: Quantum state control is essential for quantum technologies, and the authors aim to exploit dipolar interactions to create specific entangled states with circulating currents.
method: They apply quantum optimal control techniques to a system of ultracold atoms on a lattice ring, optimizing pulses to drive the system into desired entangled current states.
result: The scheme successfully generates selected states with entangled circulation, demonstrating the feasibility of using dipolar interactions for state preparation.
conclusion: The work provides a method for controlled generation of entangled current states, relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

The approach is based on collision quantum optics, where the many-body state of the waveguide is represented using discrete tim…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033109] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a matrix product state method for simulating decoherence in waveguide quantum electrodynamics, relevant to hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Waveguide QED is a key platform for hybrid quantum systems, and accurate modeling of decoherence is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The method uses collision quantum optics and matrix product states to represent the waveguide many-body state, incorporating decoherence via density matrices.
result: The approach enables efficient simulation of decoherence in waveguide QED, capturing non-Markovian effects and multiple emitters.
conclusion: The MPS method provides a powerful tool for studying realistic decoherence in waveguide QED, advancing hybrid quantum system design.

title: Free Probability In A Minimal Quantum Circuit Model
authors: Felix Fritzsch And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch and Pieter W. Claeys

Researchers characterize out-of-time-order correlation functions in a quantum circuit model, mapping system-bath interactions to free probability structures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031027] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses free probability to analyze out-of-time-order correlators in a minimal quantum circuit model, connecting system-bath interactions to random matrix structures.
motivation: Understanding the growth of quantum chaos and operator spreading in many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing. The paper aims to provide a tractable model for such dynamics.
method: The authors introduce a minimal quantum circuit model with system-bath interactions and map the dynamics to free probability theory, enabling analytical computation of OTOCs.
result: They derive exact expressions for OTOCs and show that the model exhibits universal features consistent with random matrix theory, providing insights into the emergence of chaos.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the utility of free probability in quantum circuit models, offering a new tool for studying quantum chaos and its thermodynamic implications.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, encoding the synchronized state in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, and its experimental realization in a controlled quantum platform is of high interest.
method: The authors engineer dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to achieve synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators, and they measure the synchronized state via joint measurements to access the fixed relative phase.
result: They observe synchronization between the two oscillators, confirming the predicted quantum synchronization behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a clear experimental demonstration of quantum synchronization in a trapped-ion platform, which is relevant to quantum thermodynamics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.

tldr: This review presents the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is challenging; the process tensor offers a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The paper shows that tensor-network process tensors can handle diverse physical scenarios, providing a practical tool for studying open quantum systems.
conclusion: The process tensor framework, combined with tensor networks, is a powerful approach for non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with broad applicability.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan

motivation: To demonstrate quantum computational advantage in a practical, utilizable way using a programmable ultracold-atom processor, which is a key platform in hybrid quantum systems.
method: The experiment uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, likely employing techniques such as Floquet engineering and measuring entanglement growth.
result: The processor achieves a quantum computational advantage, showing that it can simulate complex many-body dynamics beyond classical capabilities.
conclusion: This work establishes ultracold-atom processors as viable platforms for quantum simulation and computational advantage, contributing to the development of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Measurement-Induced Entanglement In Noisy 2d Random Circuits
authors: Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, And Daniel Malz
abstract:

Researchers show that noise can destroy measurement-induced entanglement in two-dimensional circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033023] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how noise affects measurement-induced entanglement in 2D random circuits, showing that noise destroys the entanglement and impacts classical hardness of simulation.
motivation: Measurement-induced entanglement in random circuits is a key phenomenon for quantum information and computational complexity, but its robustness to noise is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors analyze 2D random circuits with local measurements and noise, using numerical simulations and theoretical arguments to characterize the entanglement behavior.
result: They find that noise suppresses measurement-induced entanglement, leading to a transition in the entanglement structure and implications for the classical simulability of noisy quantum circuits.
conclusion: Noise is detrimental to measurement-induced entanglement, which must be considered for quantum advantage and error correction in noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices.

title: Fast Design And Scaling Of Multiqubit Gates In Large-Scale Trapped-Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, And Roee Ozeri
abstract:

tldr: This paper presents a polynomial-time method for designing fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates in large trapped-ion quantum computers.
motivation: Scaling trapped-ion quantum computers to hundreds of qubits requires efficient design of multiqubit gates that are both fast and robust to errors.
method: The authors develop a polynomial-time algorithm that optimizes control pulses for multiqubit entanglement gates, considering the collective motional modes of the ion crystal.
result: The method enables gate design for systems with hundreds of ions, achieving high fidelity and robustness while maintaining programmability.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable route to large-scale trapped-ion quantum computing by enabling fast and robust multiqubit gates.

title: Faster Algorithmic Quantum And Classical Simulations By Corrected Product Formulas
authors: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, and Alán Aspuru-Guzik

Injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas is shown to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with little cost increase, enabling a target accuracy to be reached with substantially lower circuit depth.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033018] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces corrected product formulas that improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with minimal overhead, reducing circuit depth for a given target accuracy.
motivation: Hamiltonian simulation is a key subroutine in quantum algorithms, and product formulas are simple but often require deep circuits. The authors aim to enhance their efficiency without significant cost.
method: They inject carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas, correcting leading error terms to achieve higher-order accuracy with little additional cost.
result: The corrected formulas enable a target accuracy to be reached with substantially lower circuit depth compared to standard product formulas, as demonstrated analytically and numerically.
conclusion: This work provides a practical improvement for Hamiltonian simulation, potentially benefiting quantum algorithms that rely on efficient simulation.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for tensor network contraction, providing polynomial-time algorithms with rigorous error bounds and exponential convergence.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is computationally hard in general, and belief propagation offers an approximate but often inaccurate method. The authors aim to improve accuracy while maintaining polynomial complexity.
method: They propose systematic corrections to belief propagation by incorporating cluster expansions, leading to a family of algorithms that refine the approximation iteratively.
result: The method achieves exponential convergence to the exact contraction result, with rigorous bounds on approximation errors, and demonstrates improved accuracy over standard belief propagation on benchmark problems.
conclusion: This work advances tensor network contraction techniques, offering a practical and theoretically grounded approach for quantum many-body simulations and quantum information tasks.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey

method: The authors analyze the properties of metastable helium-3 atoms in optical tweezers, discussing their potential for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping.
result: The paper demonstrates that helium-3's small mass provides advantages in various quantum applications, including enhanced tunneling rates and continuous-variable operations.
conclusion: Metastable helium-3 arrays offer a promising platform for quantum science, with unique features that could advance quantum computing and simulation.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that operating a neutral-atom array in a cryogenic environment extends Rydberg lifetimes by reducing blackbody radiation, thereby mitigating a key error source in two-qubit gates.
motivation: Rydberg-mediated two-qubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers are limited by finite Rydberg lifetimes, which are degraded by blackbody radiation at room temperature. Extending these lifetimes is crucial for improving gate fidelities.
method: The authors construct an optical tweezer array inside a cryogenic apparatus to shield atoms from ambient blackbody radiation, and measure Rydberg lifetimes and gate fidelities under these conditions.
result: They observe significantly extended Rydberg lifetimes and a corresponding reduction in relaxation errors, leading to improved two-qubit gate fidelities.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable and effective strategy to enhance Rydberg-based quantum computing performance by suppressing blackbody-induced decoherence.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in quantum neural networks for continual learning, showing that quantum models maintain adaptability as parameters grow.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, but quantum neural networks may offer inherent advantages. Understanding this property is crucial for developing robust quantum learning algorithms.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks in continual learning settings, comparing plasticity retention with classical counterparts. They likely use numerical simulations and theoretical analysis of parameter updates.
result: Quantum neural networks exhibit intrinsic preservation of plasticity, allowing them to learn new tasks without forgetting old ones, even as the number of parameters increases.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks provide a promising platform for continual learning due to their inherent plasticity, which could lead to more adaptive AI systems.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas

method: They decompose a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling a photonic simulator.
result: The approach allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes

motivation: Classically simulating quantum systems is generally hard, but for small subregions of expectation landscapes, efficient classical surrogates may be possible, potentially reducing quantum resource requirements.
method: The authors develop a classical surrogate model for a subregion of an expectation landscape, using initial data acquired from quantum computers to train the model.
result: They demonstrate that the classical simulation of patches of quantum landscapes can be done efficiently, with the method's performance validated on relevant examples.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach for classical simulation of quantum expectation landscapes, which could aid in quantum circuit optimization and understanding, though it is not a core information-theoretic result.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a cavity-QED model with kinetically constrained long-range interactions, revealing blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints and long-range interactions in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena, potentially relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.
method: The authors introduce a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using theoretical and numerical methods to explore the phase diagram and dynamical properties.
result: They find that kinetic constraints stabilize blockaded superradiance and lead to the emergence of long-range quantum scars, which are non-thermal eigenstates with persistent oscillations.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that cavity-QED platforms can host novel many-body phenomena, offering new avenues for exploring quantum thermodynamics and information processing in hybrid systems.

tldr: This paper introduces a novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.

method: They propose a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readouts to measure noise cross-correlations, enabling extraction of noise spectra in a previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: The method successfully bridges the intermediate-frequency gap, providing a new tool for qubit noise characterization.
