Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters can enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is challenging to achieve. The authors aim to overcome this limitation by exploiting collective effects in an ensemble.
method: They theoretically analyze a system of many emitters coupled to a cavity, focusing on two-photon interactions. They derive conditions for photon blockade and study how the collective coupling strength scales with the number of emitters.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced, leading to stronger antibunching and higher transmission as the system size increases, even when single-emitter coupling is weak.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a practical route to achieve efficient photon blockade, which is relevant for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.

abstract:

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, covering various methods and their applications across quantum physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate. A unified overview is needed to relate different approaches.
method: The paper reviews and categorizes time-propagation techniques for non-Markovian open quantum systems, highlighting commonalities and differences within a unified framework.
result: It presents a comprehensive overview of methods, including their applicability in quantum optics, quantum information, thermodynamics, and many-body physics.
conclusion: The unified framework helps researchers choose appropriate simulation methods and fosters cross-disciplinary understanding of non-Markovian dynamics.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: This review explores space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, connecting brickwork quantum circuits to solvable dynamics.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is hard; space-time duality offers a unified framework.
method: The paper is a pedagogical review, synthesizing results on space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
result: It provides a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems via space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) for decomposing multiqubit gates and implementing quantum algorithms, highlighting simplifications like the Toffoli gate.
motivation: Qudits offer potential advantages in quantum computing, such as reducing circuit complexity and enabling more efficient algorithms, but their role is not as well understood as qubits.
method: The paper surveys various qudit-qubit embeddings, discusses theoretical frameworks for gate decomposition using qudits, and reviews current experimental implementations.
result: It demonstrates that qudits can simplify certain quantum gates (e.g., Toffoli) and provides an overview of experimental progress in qudit-based quantum computing.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum information processing, with potential for simplifying circuits and enabling new algorithms, though practical challenges remain.

title: Promise Of Graph Sparsification And Decomposition For Noise Reduction In Qaoa: Analysis For Trapped-Ion Compilations
authors: Jai Moondra, Phillip C. Lotshaw, Greg Mohler, And Swati Gupta
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2185 (2026).

We develop new approximate compilation schemes that significantly reduce the expense of compiling the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) for solving the Max-Cut problem. Our main focus is on compilation with trapped-ion simulators using Pauli-[MATH] operations and all-to-all Ising Hamiltonian [MATH] evolution generated by Molmer-Sorensen or optical dipole force interactions, though some of our results also apply to standard gate-based compilations. Our results are based on principles of graph sparsification and decomposition; the former reduces the number of edges in a graph while maintaining its cut structure, while the latter breaks a weighted graph into a small number of unweighted graphs. Though these techniques have been used as heuristics in various hybrid quantum algorithms, there have been no guarantees on their performance, to the best of our knowledge. This work provides the first provable guarantees using sparsification and decomposition to improve quantum noise resilience and reduce quantum circuit complexity. For quantum hardware that uses edge-by-edge QAOA compilations, sparsification leads to a direct reduction in circuit complexity. For trapped-ion quantum simulators implementing all-to-all [MATH] pulses, we show that for a [MATH] factor loss in the Max-Cut approximation ([MATH], our compilations improve the (worst-case) number of [MATH] pulses from [MATH] to [MATH] and the (worst-case) number of Pauli-[MATH] bit flips from [MATH] to [MATH] for [MATH]-node graphs. This is an asymptotic improvement for any constant [MATH]. We demonstrate that significant improvements to the approximation ratio are obtained using decomposition in simulated trapped-ion experiments with dephasing noise. We further present a generic argument showing that sparsification results in an exponentially improved circuit fidelity lower bound in digital computing schemes based on one- and two-qubit gates, which are relevant to a wide variety of hardwares such as superconducting qubits and certain neutral atom or trapped ion setups, and more sophisticated noise models. We anticipate these approximate compilation techniques will be useful tools in a variety of future quantum computing experiments.

.
tldr: This paper provides the first provable guarantees for using graph sparsification and decomposition to reduce circuit complexity and improve noise resilience in QAOA for Max-Cut, with applications to trapped-ion and gate-based quantum computing.
motivation: QAOA compilation for Max-Cut is expensive and noise-sensitive; existing sparsification/decomposition heuristics lack theoretical guarantees. The authors aim to provide provable improvements in circuit complexity and noise resilience.
method: They develop approximate compilation schemes based on graph sparsification (reducing edges while preserving cut structure) and decomposition (breaking weighted graphs into unweighted ones), and analyze their impact on QAOA circuits for trapped-ion and gate-based hardware.
result: For trapped-ion simulators, they achieve asymptotic improvements in the number of Mølmer–Sørensen pulses and Pauli-X bit flips, with a constant-factor loss in approximation ratio. They also show exponentially improved circuit fidelity lower bounds for digital schemes.
conclusion: These techniques offer practical tools for reducing quantum circuit complexity and improving noise resilience in QAOA, with broad applicability to various quantum hardware.

title: Entanglement Growth In The Dark Intervals Of A Locally Monitored Free-fermion Chain
authors: Giovanni Di Fresco, Youenn Le Gal, Davide Valenti, Marco Schiró, And Angelo Carollo
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2183 (2026).

We consider a free fermionic chain with monitoring of the particle density on a single site of the chain and study the entanglement dynamics of quantum jump trajectories. We show that the entanglement entropy grows in time towards a stationary state which display volume law scaling of the entropy, in stark contrast with both the unitary dynamics after a local quench and the no-click limit corresponding to full post-selection. We explain the extensive entanglement growth as a consequence of the peculiar distribution of quantum jumps in time, which display superpoissonian waiting time distribution characterised by a bunching of quantum jumps followed by long dark intervals where no-clicks are detected, akin to the distribution of fluorescence light in a driven atom. We show that the presence of dark intervals is the key feature to explain the effect and that by increasing the number of sites which are monitored the volume law scaling gives away to the Zeno effect and its associated area law.

.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement growth in a free-fermion chain under local monitoring, showing that dark intervals between quantum jumps lead to volume-law entanglement, contrasting with unitary and no-click limits.
motivation: Understanding how measurement-induced dynamics affect entanglement in many-body systems is crucial for quantum information processing and thermodynamics of monitored systems.
method: The authors analyze quantum jump trajectories of a free-fermion chain with single-site density monitoring, deriving waiting time distributions and entanglement entropy scaling.
result: They find super-Poissonian waiting times with bunching and dark intervals, leading to volume-law entanglement, which transitions to area-law with more monitored sites due to Zeno effect.
conclusion: Dark intervals are key to extensive entanglement growth, providing insight into measurement-induced phases and their thermodynamic implications.

title: On The Quantum Computational Complexity Of Classical Linear Dynamics With Geometrically Local Interactions: Dequantization And Universality
authors: Kazuki Sakamoto And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2182 (2026).

The simulation of large-scale classical systems in exponentially small space on quantum computers has gained attention. The prior work demonstrated that a quantum algorithm offers an exponential speedup over any classical algorithm in simulating classical dynamics with long-range interactions. However, many real-world classical systems, such as those arising from partial differential equations, exhibit only local interactions. The question remains whether quantum algorithms can still provide exponential speedup under this condition. In this work, we thoroughly characterize the computational complexity of simulating such geometrically local systems on quantum computers. First, we dequantize the quantum algorithm for simulating short-time (polynomial-time) dynamics of such systems. This implies that the problem of simulating this dynamics does not yield any exponential quantum advantage. Second, we show that simulating short-time dynamics is at least as hard as polynomial-time and linear-space probabilistic classical computation. Third, we show that the computational complexity of simulating long-time (exponential-time) dynamics is captured by exponential-time and polynomial-space quantum computation. This suggests a super-polynomial time advantage when restricting the computation to polynomial-space, or an exponential space advantage otherwise. This work offers new insights into the complexity of classical dynamics governed by partial differential equations, providing a pathway for achieving quantum advantage in practical problems.

.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of simulating classical linear dynamics with geometrically local interactions, showing no exponential quantum advantage for short-time dynamics but potential super-polynomial advantage for long-time dynamics under space constraints.
motivation: Prior work showed exponential quantum speedup for simulating classical dynamics with long-range interactions, but real-world systems often have local interactions. The question is whether quantum advantage persists under geometric locality.
method: The authors dequantize the quantum algorithm for short-time dynamics, prove hardness results for simulating short-time dynamics, and characterize long-time dynamics complexity in terms of quantum complexity classes.
result: Short-time dynamics simulation has no exponential quantum advantage and is as hard as polynomial-time linear-space probabilistic classical computation. Long-time dynamics is captured by exponential-time polynomial-space quantum computation, suggesting super-polynomial time advantage under polynomial-space restriction.
conclusion: The work provides a thorough complexity characterization, offering insights into when quantum advantage can be achieved for simulating classical systems with local interactions.

title: Entanglement-assisted Quasi-cyclic Quantum Low-density Parity-check Codes Over Qubits
authors: Pavan Kumar, Abhi Kumar Sharma, Karthik Bharadwaj, And Shayan Srinivasa Garani
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2181 (2026).

We construct several families of entanglement-assisted quasi-cyclic quantum LDPC (EA-QC-QLDPC) codes via structured tilings of permutation matrices. The entanglement-unassisted portion of the joint Tanner graph of the proposed EA-QC-QLDPC code derived from two distinct classical QC-LDPC codes is free of 4-cycles. Notably, one of the proposed families constructed from two distinct classical codes requires only a [MATH] shared Bell pair between the quantum transmitter and receiver, highlighting its resource efficiency. We also analytically determine the exact code rates for some of the proposed constructions. Furthermore, two of the proposed families of EA-QC-QLDPC codes are derived from a single classical code whose Tanner graphs possess girth greater than six, further enhancing their error-correcting performance. We also propose an encoding scheme with improved complexity by exploiting the proposed code structure. The performance of the proposed codes is assessed under both random and burst error models under the depolarizing and Markovian noise actions. Simulation results reveal nearly one order of improvement in error-correction performance with the quaternary block-layered normalized min-sum (QBLNMS) decoder compared to the layered binary sum-product decoder over both depolarizing and Markovian channels. Using the QBLNMS decoder over a quaternary alphabet, we demonstrate that correlated Pauli errors can be effectively handled within the decoding framework. Furthermore, under the QBLNMS decoding, the proposed codes achieve [MATH] performance improvements compared to prior works and can effectively handle both random and burst errors. The code constructions are scalable across various coding rates and quantum payloads, crucial for practical quantum communication and computing systems.

.
tldr: This paper constructs entanglement-assisted quasi-cyclic quantum LDPC codes with improved error-correction performance and resource efficiency.
motivation: Quantum error correction is essential for reliable quantum communication and computation, and constructing efficient quantum LDPC codes with good performance is a key challenge.
method: The authors construct EA-QC-QLDPC codes via structured tilings of permutation matrices, ensuring 4-cycle-free Tanner graphs and deriving exact code rates. They also propose an encoding scheme and evaluate decoding with QBLNMS and layered binary sum-product decoders.
result: The proposed codes show nearly an order of magnitude improvement in error-correction performance with QBLNMS decoder over depolarizing and Markovian channels, and require only one shared Bell pair for one family.
conclusion: The scalable constructions and improved decoding performance make these codes promising for practical quantum communication and computing systems.

title: Hoare Meets Heisenberg: A Lightweight Logic For Quantum Programs
authors: Aarthi Sundaram, Robert Rand, Kartik Singhal, Youngchan Cho, And Brad Lackey
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2172 (2026).

We show that Gottesman's (1998) semantics for Clifford circuits based on the Heisenberg representation gives rise to a lightweight Hoare-like logic for efficiently characterizing a common subset of quantum programs. Our applications include (i) certifying whether auxiliary qubits can be safely disposed of, (ii) determining if a system is separable across a given bipartition, (iii) checking the transversality of a gate with respect to a given stabilizer code, and (iv) computing post-measurement states for computational basis measurements. Further, this logic is extended to accommodate universal quantum computing by deriving Hoare triples for the [MATH]-gate, multiply-controlled unitaries such as the Toffoli gate, and some gate injection circuits that use associated magic states. A number of interesting results emerge from this logic, including a lower bound on the number of [MATH] gates necessary to perform a multiply-controlled [MATH] gate.

.
tldr: This paper introduces a lightweight Hoare-like logic for quantum programs based on the Heisenberg representation, enabling efficient certification of properties like qubit disposal, separability, and gate transversality.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a practical, lightweight verification method for quantum programs, leveraging the efficiency of the Heisenberg representation for Clifford circuits.
method: They formalize a Hoare logic using Gottesman's semantics, derive Hoare triples for Clifford operations, and extend it to universal quantum computing via the T-gate, Toffoli, and magic state injection circuits.
result: The logic enables efficient certification of auxiliary qubit disposal, separability, transversality, and post-measurement states, and yields a lower bound on T-gates for multiply-controlled gates.
conclusion: The proposed logic offers a scalable verification tool for a common subset of quantum programs, with potential applications in quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Geometric Speed Limit Of State Preparation And Curved Control Spaces
authors: Maximilian Goll And Robert H. Jonsson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2160 (2026).

The preparation of quantum many-body systems faces the difficulty that in a realistic scenario only few control parameters of the system may be accessible. In this context, an interesting connection between the energy fluctuations during state preparation and its geometric length as measured by the Fubini-Study metric was discussed by Bukov et al. in 2019 [5]. An inspiring conjecture lower bounding the energy fluctuations by the minimal geometric length of all accessible state preparation protocols was put forward together with supporting examples and numerical evidence. However, we here show that the conjecture does not hold but can be violated if the accessible parameter space has extrinsic curvature, when embedded into the space of all dynamically accessible states. We illustrate this by a number of generic qubit, qutrit and harmonic oscillator systems.

.
tldr: This paper disproves a conjecture about a geometric speed limit for state preparation, showing that extrinsic curvature of the control space can lead to violations.
motivation: The authors aim to test a conjecture that energy fluctuations during state preparation are lower bounded by the minimal geometric length of accessible protocols, which would provide a fundamental speed limit.
method: They analyze the conjecture using qubit, qutrit, and harmonic oscillator systems, demonstrating counterexamples where the conjecture fails due to extrinsic curvature of the accessible parameter space.
result: The conjecture is violated in systems with curved control spaces, indicating that the geometric length alone does not capture the energy cost of state preparation.
conclusion: The geometric speed limit conjecture is not universally valid; extrinsic curvature must be considered, and new bounds are needed.

title: Near-Optimal Parameter Tuning Of Level-1 Qaoa For Ising Models
authors: V Vijendran, Dax Enshan Koh, Eunok Bae, Hyukjoon Kwon, Ping Koy Lam, And Syed M Assad
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2158 (2026).

The Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) tackles combinatorial optimisation problems by encoding their solutions into the ground state of an Ising Hamiltonian prepared by a [MATH]-level parameterised circuit, with the angles tuned classically. Parameter optimisation is widely regarded as a central bottleneck, even for the shallowest circuits. Focusing on QAOA at [MATH] (QAOA[MATH]), we show that tuning the two angles [MATH] for weighted Ising models is not a black-box search but a structured signal-processing problem. We prove that the QAOA[MATH] expectation value is a partial Fourier series in [MATH] whose frequencies are determined explicitly by the problem's couplings and fields, giving instance-wise bandwidth bounds and, via the Nyquist–Shannon theorem, the sampling resolution needed to avoid the aliasing that causes coarse-grid searches to return spurious optima. We then eliminate the mixer angle analytically, computing [MATH] in closed form to reduce the search to one dimension, and apply a subdivision algorithm that locates the globally optimal [MATH] in polynomial time with a certificate of optimality when the weights are commensurable and bounded. For regular weighted graphs, we further prove the conventional wisdom that the globally optimal [MATH] concentrates near zero and coincides with the first local optimum, giving a rigorous account of the empirical success of small-angle initialisation and allowing gradient descent to replace exhaustive line searches. Validated within Recursive QAOA (RQAOA) on weighted instances of 128 and 256 qubits, our method consistently outperforms both coarsely optimised RQAOA and semidefinite programming.

.
tldr: This paper provides a rigorous analysis of QAOA parameter optimization for Ising models, showing that the expectation value is a partial Fourier series and deriving optimal sampling and initialization strategies.
motivation: Parameter optimization is a central bottleneck in QAOA, and the authors aim to replace black-box search with a structured signal-processing approach.
method: They prove the QAOA1 expectation value is a partial Fourier series with explicit frequencies, eliminate the mixer angle analytically, and apply a subdivision algorithm for global optimization. They also prove concentration of optimal angles near zero for regular graphs.
result: The method outperforms coarsely optimized RQAOA and semidefinite programming on weighted instances of 128 and 256 qubits.
conclusion: QAOA parameter tuning can be made efficient and provably optimal under certain conditions, providing a rigorous foundation for practical optimization.

title: Spin-based True Random Number Generation Enabled By Voltage-amplified Quantum Fluctuations
authors: Jie Zheng, Jiyong Kang, Zheng Zhu, Di Wu, Yuesheng Li, Dongxing Yu, Jiayong Wang, Hongxing Xu And Chenglong Jia
abstract: We investigate spin quantum-fluctuation effects that originate from the Heisenberg uncertainty principle during the dynamical cycle of disentanglement, entanglement, and re-disentanglement between itinerant electrons and localized magnetic moments mediated by the s–d exchange interaction. Beyond conventional deterministic spin-transfer torque, we analyze an intrinsic mechanism that transfers spin quantum fluctuations to a nanomagnet. By extending the Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert equation to incorporate both quantum and thermal stochastic fields, we identify a temperature regime in which quantum fluctuations dominate the magnetization dynamics. We further show that voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy exponentially amplifies spin quantum fluctuations, enabling binary readout through magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions. These findings provide a microscopic framework for fluctuation-driven spin dynamics and outline a device-level pathway toward spin-based quantum true random number generation.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for true random number generation based on spin quantum fluctuations amplified by voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy, extending the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation to include quantum stochastic fields.
motivation: To provide a microscopic framework for fluctuation-driven spin dynamics and a device-level pathway for quantum true random number generation, leveraging quantum fluctuations beyond thermal noise.
method: The authors extend the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation to incorporate both quantum and thermal stochastic fields, and analyze the dynamics of a nanomagnet under s-d exchange interaction, showing that voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy exponentially amplifies spin quantum fluctuations.
result: They identify a temperature regime where quantum fluctuations dominate magnetization dynamics, and demonstrate that binary readout is possible via magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, enabling spin-based quantum true random number generation.
conclusion: The findings provide a microscopic framework for fluctuation-driven spin dynamics and outline a device-level pathway for spin-based quantum true random number generation, which has implications for information processing and thermodynamics.

title: Sparse Identification Of Quantum Hamiltonian Dynamics Via Quantum Circuit Learning
authors: Yusei Tateyama And Yuzuru Kato
abstract: Sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy) is a data-driven framework for estimating classical nonlinear dynamical systems from time-series data. In this approach, system dynamics is represented as a linear combination of a predefined set of basis functions, and the corresponding coefficients are sparsely estimated from observed time-series data. In this study, we propose sparse identification of quantum Hamiltonian dynamics (SIQHDy), a SINDy-inspired quantum circuit learning framework for estimating quantum Hamiltonian dynamics from time-series data of quantum measurement outcomes. In SIQHDy, the unitary evolution of a quantum Hamiltonian system is expressed as a product of basis quantum circuits, and the corresponding circuit parameters are estimated through sparsity-promoting optimization. We numerically demonstrate that SIQHDy accurately reconstructs the dynamics of single-, three-, and five-spin systems, and exhibits robustness to measurement noise in the three-spin case. Furthermore, we propose an extension of SIQHDy for scenarios with limited accessible observables and evaluate its performance in identifying three-spin systems and in network-structure identification for five-spin systems.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum circuit learning framework inspired by SINDy to sparsely identify quantum Hamiltonian dynamics from measurement time-series data.
motivation: Estimating quantum Hamiltonian dynamics from data is crucial for characterizing quantum systems, but existing methods may require many measurements or lack interpretability. The authors aim to adapt classical sparse identification techniques to quantum systems.
method: The method, SIQHDy, represents the unitary evolution as a product of basis quantum circuits and estimates circuit parameters via sparsity-promoting optimization, with an extension for limited observables.
result: Numerical demonstrations show accurate reconstruction of single-, three-, and five-spin systems, robustness to noise in three-spin case, and successful network-structure identification for five-spin systems.
conclusion: SIQHDy provides a promising data-driven approach for identifying quantum Hamiltonian dynamics, potentially useful for quantum system characterization and network inference.

title: Rotation-enhanced Photonic Spin Hall Effect In A Ring Bose–Einstein Condensate
authors: Leibo Deng, Muqaddar Abbas, Ghaisud Din, Hocine Bahlouli And Yong-Hong Ma
abstract: We show that rotation can strongly amplify the photonic spin Hall effect in a ring Bose–Einstein condensate. For an incident probe beam carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM), the spin-dependent transverse shift of the reflected light is weak in the non-rotating regime but becomes strongly enhanced under rotation because rotation lifts the degeneracy of the condensate mechanical modes via Bragg scattering. The resulting mode splitting produces large photonic spin Hall shifts at ultra-low optical power, with the enhancement increasing with both the condensate winding number and the probe OAM , while remaining weakly affected by atom–atom interactions. Our findings elucidate a rotation-governed mechanism underlying spin-dependent light transport in hybrid atom–optomechanical systems, thereby highlighting its potential for applications in high-precision rotational sensing.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that rotation can strongly enhance the photonic spin Hall effect in a ring Bose-Einstein condensate, enabling large spin-dependent shifts at ultra-low optical power.
motivation: The photonic spin Hall effect is typically weak, and the authors aim to find a mechanism to amplify it for applications in precision sensing.
method: They theoretically analyze a ring BEC system where rotation lifts degeneracy of mechanical modes via Bragg scattering, leading to mode splitting that enhances the spin Hall shift.
result: The enhancement increases with condensate winding number and probe OAM, while being weakly affected by atom-atom interactions.
conclusion: The findings reveal a rotation-governed mechanism for spin-dependent light transport, with potential for high-precision rotational sensing.

title: Fate Of Entanglement In Open Quantum Spin Liquid: Time Evolution Of Its Genuine Multipartite Negativity Upon Sudden Coupling To A Dissipative Bosonic Environment
authors: Federico Garcia-Gaitan And Branislav K Nikolić
abstract: Many-body entanglement properties of quantum spin liquids (QSLs), persisting at arbitrarily long distances, have been intensely explored over the past two decades, but mostly for QSLs viewed as closed quantum systems. However, in experiments and potential quantum computing applications, candidate materials for this exotic phase of quantum matter will always interact with a dissipative environment, such as the one generated by bosonic quasiparticles in solids at finite temperature. Here we investigate both the stability and spatial distribution of entanglement for the Kitaev model of QSL, which is made open by its sudden coupling to an infinite bosonic bath of Caldeira–Leggett type and then time-evolved in both Markovian and non-Markovian regimes. From the time-dependent density matrix of QSL subregions, we extract genuine multipartite negativity (GMN), quantum Fisher information, spin–spin correlators, and the expectation value (EV) of the Wilson loop operator. In particular, time dependence of GMN offers the most penetrating insights: (i) in the Markovian regime, it remains nonzero only in hexagonal loopy subregions of QSL (as also discovered very recently for closed QSLs), eventually vanishing on the same timescale on which the EV of the Wilson loop operator vanishes; (ii) in the non-Markovian regime with pronounced memory effects, surprisingly, GMN remains nonzero up to much higher temperatures. In addition, the non-Markovian dynamics generates emergent interactions between spins, thereby opening avenues for tailoring properties of QSL via engineering of dissipation.
tldr: This paper studies the time evolution of genuine multipartite negativity in an open Kitaev quantum spin liquid coupled to a dissipative bosonic environment, revealing that non-Markovian dynamics preserves entanglement at higher temperatures.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are typically studied as closed systems, but real applications involve dissipative environments. Understanding how entanglement behaves under such conditions is crucial for quantum computing and fundamental physics.
method: The authors model the Kitaev QSL coupled to a Caldeira-Leggett bosonic bath and simulate time evolution in Markovian and non-Markovian regimes. They compute genuine multipartite negativity, quantum Fisher information, spin-spin correlators, and Wilson loop expectation values from the time-dependent density matrix.
result: In the Markovian regime, GMN persists only in hexagonal loopy subregions and vanishes on the same timescale as the Wilson loop. In the non-Markovian regime, GMN remains nonzero up to much higher temperatures, and emergent interactions are generated.
conclusion: Non-Markovian dissipation can stabilize multipartite entanglement in QSLs, suggesting that engineering dissipation could tailor QSL properties for applications.

title: High-Efficiency Loading Of 2400 Ytterbium Atoms In Optical Tweezer Arrays
authors: Jiawen Zhu, Changfeng Chen, Li Zhou, Xiangru Xie, Chenyang Jiang, Zhuoli Ding, Fan Wu, Fan Yang, Guoqing Wang, Qihuang Gong, Peng Zhang, Sheng Zhang, And Pai Peng
abstract:
Author(s): Jiawen Zhu, Changfeng Chen, Li Zhou, Xiangru Xie, Chenyang Jiang, Zhuoli Ding, Fan Wu, Fan Yang, Guoqing Wang, Qihuang Gong, Peng Zhang, Sheng Zhang, and Pai Peng

Using a technique applicable to other atomic species, the stable loading of 2400 neutral Ytterbium-174 atoms in an optical tweezer array represents the largest alkaline-earth-like atom array to date.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 063201] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates stable loading of 2400 Ytterbium-174 atoms in an optical tweezer array, the largest alkaline-earth-like atom array to date.
motivation: Scaling up neutral atom arrays is crucial for quantum computing and simulation, and alkaline-earth atoms offer unique advantages. The authors aim to achieve high-efficiency loading of a large array.
method: They use a technique applicable to other atomic species, likely involving optical tweezers and efficient loading from a magneto-optical trap, to assemble a 2400-atom array.
result: They successfully load 2400 Ytterbium-174 atoms with high efficiency, setting a record for alkaline-earth-like atom arrays.
conclusion: The demonstrated loading technique and array size advance the capabilities for quantum information processing with neutral atoms, particularly for alkaline-earth species.

title: Energy Gap Of Quantum Spin Glasses: A Projection Quantum Monte Carlo Study
authors: L. Brodoloni, G. E. Astrakharchik, S. Giorgini, And S. Pilati
abstract:
Author(s): L. Brodoloni, G. E. Astrakharchik, S. Giorgini, and S. Pilati

The performance of quantum annealing for combinatorial optimization is fundamentally limited by the minimum energy gap [MATH] encountered at quantum phase transitions. We investigate the scaling of [MATH] with system size [MATH] for two paradigmatic quantum spin-glass models: the two-dimens…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060403] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the scaling of the minimum energy gap in quantum spin glasses using projection quantum Monte Carlo, relevant to quantum annealing performance.
motivation: Quantum annealing performance is limited by the minimum energy gap at quantum phase transitions; understanding its scaling is crucial for optimization.
method: The authors use projection quantum Monte Carlo simulations to compute the energy gap for two-dimensional quantum spin-glass models.
result: They find that the gap scales exponentially with system size, indicating a first-order transition and limiting adiabatic performance.
conclusion: The results highlight the challenges for quantum annealing in these models and suggest the need for alternative approaches.

title: Simultaneous Nonreciprocal Unconventional Photon Blockades Via Two Degenerate Optical Parametric Amplifiers In Spinning Resonators
authors: J. X. Yang, Zi-Lin Zhao, Ze Wang, T. Z. Luan, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, And H. Z. Shen
abstract:
Author(s): J. X. Yang, Zi-Lin Zhao, Ze Wang, T. Z. Luan, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, and H. Z. Shen

We present a scheme to realize simultaneous nonreciprocal unconventional photon blockades in a system of two coupled spinning resonators (modes [MATH] and [MATH]), each embedded with a degenerate optical parametric amplifier (DOPA). The rotation of the resonators induces opposite Sagnac-Fizeau shifts for …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023703] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme for simultaneous nonreciprocal unconventional photon blockades using two coupled spinning resonators with degenerate optical parametric amplifiers.
motivation: To achieve nonreciprocal photon blockade, which is important for quantum information processing and chiral quantum networks.
method: The system consists of two coupled spinning resonators, each with a degenerate optical parametric amplifier, and the rotation induces Sagnac-Fizeau shifts. The unconventional photon blockade is achieved via quantum interference.
result: The scheme enables simultaneous nonreciprocal unconventional photon blockades, allowing for direction-dependent photon statistics.
conclusion: The proposed system provides a feasible platform for realizing nonreciprocal single-photon devices, which could be useful for quantum networks.

title: Universal Scaling Of Quantum Caustics In The Dynamics Of Interacting Particles
authors: Monalisa Singh Roy, Jesse Mumford, Amit Ozer, Oded Porat, D. H. J. O'dell, And Emanuele G. Dalla Torre
abstract:
Author(s): Monalisa Singh Roy, Jesse Mumford, Amit Ozer, Oded Porat, D. H. J. O'Dell, and Emanuele G. Dalla Torre

Recent theoretical studies have predicted the existence of caustics in many-body quantum dynamics, where they manifest as extended regions of enhanced probability density that obey temporal and spatial scaling relations. Focusing on the transverse-field Ising model, we investigate the dynamics initi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022201] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies universal scaling of quantum caustics in the transverse-field Ising model, connecting many-body quantum dynamics to wave phenomena.
motivation: To understand universal features of many-body quantum dynamics, specifically the emergence of caustics as enhanced probability density regions with scaling relations.
method: The authors analyze the transverse-field Ising model, likely using analytical and numerical methods to study the dynamics of interacting particles and identify caustic structures.
result: They find universal scaling behavior of quantum caustics, with temporal and spatial scaling relations that are independent of microscopic details.
conclusion: The work reveals universal aspects of quantum many-body dynamics, potentially linking to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Preparation Of A Quasi-two-dimensional Bose Mixture Of Ultracold $^{23}\mathrm{Na}$ And $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$ Atoms
authors: Ji-Kai Liao, Hao-Ran Zhang, Xiao-Rong Yu, Ya-Qun Qi, Yi-Cheng Guo, Bo Zhao, Jun Rui, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Ji-Kai Liao, Hao-Ran Zhang, Xiao-Rong Yu, Ya-Qun Qi, Yi-Cheng Guo, Bo Zhao, Jun Rui, and Jian-Wei Pan

Quantum gases confined in reduced dimensions have enabled the observation of many exotic quantum phenomena. While existing experiments primarily focus on homonuclear systems, we report here on the efficient preparation of a quasi-two-dimensional heteronuclear quantum degenerate mixture of ultracold …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023303] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the efficient preparation of a quasi-two-dimensional heteronuclear quantum degenerate mixture of ultracold sodium and rubidium atoms.
motivation: To extend studies of quantum gases in reduced dimensions to heteronuclear systems, which can offer new physics due to mass imbalance and interactions.
method: The authors use a combination of laser cooling, magnetic trapping, and evaporative cooling to create a degenerate mixture of 23Na and 87Rb in a quasi-2D geometry, likely using an optical lattice or a highly oblate trap.
result: They achieve efficient preparation of the quasi-2D heteronuclear quantum degenerate mixture, demonstrating the feasibility of such systems.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for exploring novel quantum phenomena in heteronuclear quasi-2D systems, with potential applications in quantum simulation and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Thermodynamic Phase Transitions In Lattice Spin Systems With Severe Kinetic Constraints: Numerical Simulation Results
authors: Ruifeng Liu, Jianwen Zhou, Yejia Chen, Jiahang Chen, And Hai-Jun Zhou

title: Disorder-Induced Entanglement Phase Transitions In Non-Hermitian Systems With Skin Effects
authors: Kai Li, Ze-Chuan Liu, And Yong Xu
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2186 (2026).

Non-Hermitian dynamics is ubiquitous in various physical systems. While recent study shows that such a dynamics leads to an area-law scaling of the entanglement entropy due to the non-Hermitian skin effects, it remains unclear how disorder changes the behavior of the entanglement entropy in a non-Hermitian system with skin effects. Here we study the dynamics of a many-body state of free fermions in the paradigmatic Hatano-Nelson model with open boundaries, and find that the area-law behavior of the entanglement entropy in the pristine Hatano-Nelson model develops into a logarithmic scaling for small disorder strength. As we further increase the disorder strength, the system reenters an area-law regime through an entanglement phase transition. At the critical point, the entanglement entropy exhibits a universal algebraic scaling. We further demonstrate the absence of a conformal invariance in the log-law regime by examining the subsystem entanglement entropy, the connected correlation function and the mutual information. Finally, we show the existence of disorder induced entanglement phase transitions in the Hatano-Nelson model with periodic boundaries.

.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement phase transitions in a non-Hermitian Hatano-Nelson model with disorder, showing transitions between area-law and logarithmic scaling.
motivation: To understand how disorder affects entanglement entropy in non-Hermitian systems with skin effects, which is relevant to quantum dynamics and thermodynamics.
method: The authors numerically study the dynamics of free fermions in the Hatano-Nelson model with open and periodic boundaries, varying disorder strength and measuring entanglement entropy, correlation functions, and mutual information.
result: They find that small disorder induces a logarithmic scaling of entanglement entropy, while stronger disorder restores area-law behavior, with a universal algebraic scaling at the critical point. They also show absence of conformal invariance in the log-law regime.
conclusion: Disorder induces entanglement phase transitions in non-Hermitian systems with skin effects, which may have implications for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.

title: Atommovr: An Open-source Simulation Framework For Rearrangement In Atomic Arrays
authors: Nikhil K Harle, Bo-Yu Chen, Bob Bao, And Hannes Bernien
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2177 (2026).

The task of atom rearrangement has emerged in the last decade as a fundamental building block in the development of neutral atom-based quantum processors. As such processors grow to thousands of atoms, it becomes increasingly important to design algorithms robust to experimental sources of error. While recent progress has been made towards developing algorithms with favorable time scaling, such work has been limited to noiseless settings. Moreover, there is a lack of open-source code for reproducing and benchmarking existing algorithms. To address these deficiencies, we develop an open-source simulation framework, atommovr, and leverage it to study three distinct settings: 1) time-optimal, noiseless rearrangement, 2) noisy rearrangement under realistic error models, and 3) noiseless dual-species rearrangement. We extract lower bounds for time-optimal rearrangement, study advantageous strategies across different error regimes, and develop a novel dual-species algorithm, InsideOut, capable of avoiding 'blocked' configurations with a near-unity success rate. We hope that atommovr can serve as a common tool for the community to study rearrangement, lower the barrier to entry for new experimental groups, and stimulate progress in developing algorithms tailored to minimize atom loss in experiment.

.
tldr: This paper introduces an open-source simulation framework for atom rearrangement in neutral atom arrays, focusing on algorithm benchmarking and development under noisy and dual-species settings.
motivation: As neutral atom quantum processors scale to thousands of atoms, efficient and robust rearrangement algorithms are crucial, yet existing work lacks open-source tools and noise-aware studies.
method: The authors develop the atommovr simulation framework and use it to analyze time-optimal noiseless rearrangement, noisy rearrangement with realistic error models, and noiseless dual-species rearrangement, including a novel algorithm called InsideOut.
result: They extract lower bounds for time-optimal rearrangement, identify advantageous strategies across error regimes, and demonstrate that InsideOut avoids blocked configurations with near-unity success rate.
conclusion: The framework provides a common benchmarking tool for the community, lowering entry barriers and stimulating progress in atom-loss-minimizing algorithms.

title: Exact Quantum Many-Body Scars In 2d Quantum Gauge Models
authors: Yuan Miao, Linhao Li, Hosho Katsura, And Masahito Yamazaki
abstract:

Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) serve as important examples of ergodicity-breaking phenomena in quantum many-body systems. Despite recent extensive studies, exact QMBS are rare in dimensions higher than one. In this paper, we study a two-dimensional quantum [MATH] gauge model that is dual to a two-dimensional spin-[MATH] XY model defined on bipartite graphs. We identify the exact eigenstates of the XY model with a tower structure as exact QMBS. Exploiting the duality transformation, we show that the exact QMBS of the XY model (and XXZ model) after the transformation are the exact QMBS of the dual [MATH] gauge model. This construction is versatile and has potential applications for finding new QMBS in other higher-dimensional models.

motivation: Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) are rare in dimensions higher than one, and this work aims to find exact QMBS in a 2D gauge model, which could deepen understanding of ergodicity breaking.
method: The authors study a 2D quantum gauge model dual to a spin-1/2 XY model on bipartite graphs, identify exact eigenstates with a tower structure in the XY model, and use the duality transformation to map them to QMBS in the gauge model.
result: They demonstrate that the exact QMBS of the XY model (and XXZ model) become exact QMBS of the dual gauge model, providing a versatile construction for finding QMBS in higher-dimensional models.
conclusion: The construction offers a new route to exact QMBS in higher dimensions, potentially applicable to other models, but the direct relevance to the user's research interests is limited.

Coulomb crystals form when the Coulomb interaction between charged particles dominates over kinetic energy; the prototype is the Wigner crystal formed by conduction electrons in metals at low densities. In recent years, it has become possible to realize Coulomb crystals using laser-cooled trapped ions, and these systems allow for unprecedented control of experimental parameters. This review describes the state of the art of ion Coulomb crystals in one, two, and three dimensions, their properties in and out of equilibrium, and their importance across fields ranging from condensed matter to astrophysics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 035001] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.

motivation: The paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of ion Coulomb crystals, highlighting their tunability and relevance to condensed matter and astrophysics.
method: It is a review article summarizing experimental and theoretical progress on ion Coulomb crystals in 1D, 2D, and 3D, including equilibrium and non-equilibrium properties.
result: The review synthesizes the state of the art, discussing structural phases, dynamics, and applications across fields.
conclusion: Ion Coulomb crystals are a versatile platform for studying many-body physics, but the paper's focus is not aligned with the user's research directions.

authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review covers tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution, a technique in nanoscale optical imaging.
motivation: The paper aims to summarize recent advances in tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy, which combines scanning probe techniques with optical fluorescence to achieve superresolution beyond the diffraction limit.
method: It reviews the principles and experimental implementations of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence, focusing on the use of a scanning tip as a nanoscale optical antenna to confine electromagnetic fields.
result: The review highlights that this technique can achieve atomic-scale spatial resolution and provides insights into molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy is a powerful tool for studying molecules at the atomic scale, with potential applications in materials science and chemistry.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
